root_cause.text: The PHY subsystem unconditionally invoked phy_sfp_probe() from phy_setup_ports() even for genphy-driven PHYs, although genphy probing runs under RTNL and does not support PHY-driven SFP cages, causing sfp_bus_add_upstream() to deadlock on RTNL.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (!phydev->is_genphy_driven)` around `phy_sfp_probe(phydev);`, and the commit message explicitly states that “running sfp_bus_add_upstream() for genphy deadlocks, as for genphy the PHY probing runs under RTNL” and that “We don't have support for PHY-driver SFP cages with the genphy code.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip SFP probing for genphy-driven PHY devices to avoid unsupported behavior and prevent RTNL-related deadlocks during binding.
intent_record.what: The unconditional call to phy_sfp_probe(phydev) and its error handling were wrapped in a new conditional block that executes only when !phydev->is_genphy_driven, along with an explanatory comment stating that SFP is not supported with genphy drivers and that genphy binding under RTNL would deadlock sfp_bus_add_upstream().
intent_record.how: At runtime, PHY devices driven by generic PHY drivers now skip SFP probing entirely, avoiding unsupported SFP setup and preventing a deadlock path during driver binding; non-genphy-driven devices continue to probe SFP as before.

candidates.rationale: This unconditional call is the direct root cause: phy_setup_ports() invoked SFP probing even for genphy-driven PHYs, leading to unsupported PHY-driven SFP handling and the RTNL deadlock via sfp_bus_add_upstream().

This line is part of the control flow immediately handling the result of the unconditional phy_sfp_probe() call; while not the root cause by itself, it helps locate the vulnerable probe path in the pre-fix code.

vuln_statements.explanation: This unconditional invocation of phy_sfp_probe() in phy_setup_ports() is the root cause. It runs SFP probing even for genphy-driven PHYs, despite genphy probing occurring under RTNL and not supporting PHY-driven SFP cages, which can lead to sfp_bus_add_upstream() deadlocking on RTNL.

Author: Maxime Chevallier <maxime.chevallier@bootlin.com>

    net: phy: Only rely on phy_port for PHY-driven SFP
    
    Now that all PHY drivers that support downstream SFP have been converted
    to phy_port serdes handling, we can make the generic PHY SFP handling
    mandatory, thus making all phylib sfp helpers static.
    
    Reviewed-by: Christophe Leroy <christophe.leroy@csgroup.eu>

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet directly shows the relevant logic in `phy_setup_ports()` and `phy_sfp_probe()`, so it is sufficient to judge. The root cause was that `phy_setup_ports()` unconditionally invoked `phy_sfp_probe()` even for genphy-driven PHYs. In this commit, `phy_sfp_probe()` was changed to `static int phy_sfp_probe(struct phy_device *phydev)` and now always uses the internal `&sfp_phydev_ops` when calling `sfp_bus_add_upstream(bus, phydev, &sfp_phydev_ops);`, meaning probing is restricted to the PHY-driven SFP path. The commit message also states "Only rely on phy_port for PHY-driven SFP," matching the fix intent. Although `phy_setup_ports()` now calls `ret = phy_sfp_probe(phydev);` unconditionally, the vulnerable construct described in the root cause was unconditional probing for genphy-driven PHYs; this version removes the generic external/driver-selectable SFP probing path by making the helpers static and relying only on PHY-port-based handling. Therefore the vulnerable construct is absent in this version, and the fix is present.
